sources.title: Calculator clinical-safety governance record
limitations: Records the release decision and does not replace an instrument source.

sources.title: The PHQ-9: Validity of a Brief Depression Severity Measure
limitations: A completed score supports assessment and monitoring; it is not a diagnosis or management decision.

sources.title: A Brief Measure for Assessing Generalized Anxiety Disorder
limitations: A completed score supports anxiety assessment and does not establish a diagnosis.

sources.title: Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10)
limitations: The K10 measures psychological distress and is not a diagnostic category.

sources.title: Detecting alcoholism: The CAGE questionnaire
limitations: CAGE is a lifetime problem-drinking screen and does not assess current use or withdrawal.

sources.title: The AUDIT alcohol consumption questions (AUDIT-C): an effective brief screening test for problem drinking
limitations: Derived in a United States Veterans Affairs general medical clinic sample from which women were excluded, so it does not support a threshold for women.
A completed score screens reported consumption and is not a diagnosis or management decision.

sources.issuer: Bradley, DeBenedetti, Volk, Williams, Frank & Kivlahan
sources.title: AUDIT-C as a brief screen for alcohol misuse in primary care
sources.version: 2007 validation study (Alcohol Clin Exp Res 31(7):1208-17, doi:10.1111/j.1530-0277.2007.00403.x)
limitations: Thresholds of 4 or more for men and 3 or more for women were derived in a United States academic family-practice sample, not an Australian one.
Optimal thresholds vary by population and setting, so the convention in use must be stated rather than assumed.

sources.title: Australian standard drinks guide
limitations: Supports Australian standard-drink context for the item wording only.
Does not validate AUDIT-C, support any screening threshold, or establish a diagnosis or management decision.

sources.title: Development and validation of a screening instrument for bipolar spectrum disorder
limitations: Quarantined pending approval of digital-use rights and completion semantics.

sources.title: Evaluation of suicidal patients: the SAD PERSONS scale
limitations: Not released for active score-based clinical decision support.

sources.title: The Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale. I. Development, Use, and Reliability
limitations: Quarantined because the current generic anchors are not a verified Y-BOCS implementation.

sources.title: Pfizer to offer free public access to mental health assessment tools
limitations: States that PHQ and GAD-7 are available without copyright restriction and at no charge; does not permit changing validated wording or scoring.

sources.title: K10 and K6 Scales — permission requests
limitations: Use is free without formal permission, but the author retains copyright and requests citation plus copyright acknowledgement.

sources.issuer: John A. Ewing / Bowles Center for Alcohol Studies
sources.title: CAGE Questionnaire permission statement
limitations: Allows clinical and research use with citation; a profit-making endeavour requires a negotiated payment with the Center.

sources.title: AUDIT use-rights frequently asked questions
limitations: No permission is needed only for non-commercial use; the questionnaire must not be materially changed and must be identified as WHO-approved.

claims.text: A completed PHQ-9 total of 0-27 grades depressive symptom severity and supports case-finding and monitoring. The total alone does not establish a diagnosis or a management decision.
claims.population: Adults assessed with the original 9-item form
claims.supportLocator: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2001, scoring and criterion-validity sections.

claims.text: An endorsed response to the thoughts-of-death-or-self-harm item requires direct and timely clinical assessment. It is a prompt to assess, not a risk score or a prediction of self-harm.
claims.supportLocator: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2001, item 9; local clinical-safety release decision.

claims.text: A completed GAD-7 total of 0-21 grades anxiety symptom severity and screens for generalised anxiety disorder. It is not a stand-alone diagnostic assessment.
claims.population: Adults assessed with the original 7-item form
claims.supportLocator: Spitzer, Kroenke, Williams & Lowe 2006, scoring and validity sections.

claims.text: A completed K10 total of 10-50 describes non-specific psychological distress over the past 4 weeks. Distress bands are not diagnostic categories and K10 is one of several accepted outcome measures rather than a required instrument.
claims.supportLocator: Australian Bureau of Statistics 2003 K10 information paper, scoring and population-band sections.

claims.text: A completed CAGE screens for lifetime alcohol problems. It does not quantify current consumption, stage dependence, or assess alcohol withdrawal.
A completed AUDIT-C total of 0-12 screens reported alcohol consumption for heavy drinking and possible alcohol use disorder. A score does not itself diagnose dependence or determine management.
claims.population: Adults in general medical and primary care settings
claims.supportLocator: Bush et al. 1998, AUROC and screening-performance results for the three AUDIT consumption items.

claims.text: The screening convention registered for this tool is Bradley et al. 2007: a total of 4 or more for men and 3 or more for women. These thresholds were derived in United States primary care, so the convention in use must be named rather than assumed, and a total of 3 is positive for women but not for men.
claims.population: Adult men and women in primary care
claims.supportLocator: Bradley et al. 2007, sensitivity and specificity by sex at the reported thresholds.

claims.text: An Australian standard drink contains 10 g of alcohol, which is the unit the AUDIT-C item wording assumes. This supports drink-size context only and supports neither AUDIT-C validation nor any screening threshold.
claims.population: Australian drinkers and clinicians applying Australian standard-drink measures
claims.supportLocator: Australian Government Department of Health standard drinks guide, standard-drink definition.

claims.text: A positive MDQ screen on the original form requires the symptom-count threshold plus symptom co-occurrence plus moderate-or-serious functional impairment. Screening performance depends on population and setting, and a negative screen cannot by itself exclude bipolar disorder.
claims.supportLocator: Hirschfeld et al. 2000, three-criterion scoring rule and reported sensitivity and specificity.

claims.text: SAD PERSONS must not be used to stratify suicide risk, predict suicide, or drive admission or discharge decisions. It is retained only as a quarantined record of static risk factors.
claims.population: Not for active use in any population
claims.supportLocator: Patterson et al. 1983 derivation, read with the local not-for-active-use release decision.

claims.text: Y-BOCS severity interpretation is specific to an exact edition, administration method and anchor set. Original Y-BOCS and Y-BOCS-II are distinct instruments and their severity conventions must not be substituted for one another.
claims.population: Adults with obsessive-compulsive disorder, original interviewer-administered form
claims.supportLocator: Goodman et al. 1989, development, administration and severity-rating sections.

claims.text: Pfizer's published statement permits reproduction, translation, display and distribution of the PHQ-9 without further permission, with attribution. Reuse permission does not establish that altered wording remains validated.
claims.population: Not population specific; applies to reproduction of the instrument
claims.supportLocator: Pfizer public-access statement for the PHQ and GAD-7 instruments.

claims.text: Pfizer's published statement permits reproduction, translation, display and distribution of the GAD-7 without further permission, with attribution. Reuse permission does not establish that altered wording remains validated.
claims.population: Not population specific; applies to reproduction of the instrument
claims.supportLocator: Pfizer public-access statement for the PHQ and GAD-7 instruments.

claims.text: K10 may be used without formal approval while copyright is retained, with citation and copyright acknowledgement required. Permitted translations and timeframe variants are separate questions from validation of any adaptation.
claims.population: Not population specific; applies to reproduction of the instrument
claims.supportLocator: Kessler K10 and K6 permission-requests statement.

claims.text: The CAGE permission statement allows clinical and research use and qualifies profit-making use separately, which requires negotiated permission.
claims.population: Not population specific; applies to reproduction of the instrument
claims.supportLocator: CAGE questionnaire permission statement, clinical/research and profit-making clauses.

claims.text: The AUDIT use-rights statement permits non-commercial use without material change and requires the instrument to be identified as WHO-approved. It does not by itself grant commercial use or permit altered wording.
claims.population: Not population specific; applies to reproduction of the instrument
claims.supportLocator: WHO AUDIT use-rights frequently asked questions, non-commercial-use and alteration clauses.
